---
title: "Bill of materials"
---

Every critical component is offered at three price points. **Budget** gets a
working single-tone canceller for the cost of a nice dinner party; **Mid** is
the recommended build meeting every spec requirement with margin;
**Reference** is the no-compromise version. Tiers mix freely — the categories
are independent. The plan actually being built is the
[**Selected build**](#selected-build) below, with its
[supporting items](#supporting-items); equipment placement is on the
[Layout](layout.qmd) page.

US street prices **as of October 2026**, from the linked retailer/aggregator
listings; prices drift, so re-check before ordering. All actuators are
*powered* subwoofers (amplification included), and all interfaces listed
supply the +48 V phantom power the electret measurement mics need.

## 1. Controller platform

Runs the multichannel FxLMS loop. The tonal controller is computationally
trivial (a few weights per tone per actuator at a 2–4 kHz effective rate), so
almost anything works; what matters is a stable real-time audio stack.

| Tier | Product | Price | Notes |
|------|---------|------:|-------|
| Budget | Any existing laptop/PC, Linux + PipeWire/JACK | $0 | Repurposed hardware; fully adequate for the DSP load. |
| Mid | N100/N150-class fanless mini-PC (Beelink Mini S12 Pro or similar), Linux `PREEMPT_RT` | ~$160–230 | Dedicated, silent, headless; runs 24/7. |
| Reference | NUC-class fanless mini-PC (ASUS NUC 14 Essential or similar), Linux `PREEMPT_RT` | ~$350–450 | Headroom for simultaneous logging, web dashboard, and re-identification. |

An embedded platform (Bela, Teensy + audio shield) is a fine alternative for
a sealed appliance-style build, but standard boards are stereo-limited;
multichannel I/O is simpler over USB on a Linux box. (Raspberry Pi 5 was
dropped: the 2025–26 memory-price surge pushed the 8 GB board above
mini-PC territory.)

## 2. Multichannel audio interface

Needs ≥ 4 mic inputs with phantom power and ≥ 2 (goal 4) line outputs,
simultaneously. Round-trip latency is absorbed into the identified secondary
path (see [spec](spec.qmd#rates-and-latency)), so even budget USB interfaces
qualify.

| Tier | Product | I/O | Price |
|------|---------|-----|------:|
| Budget | [Behringer U-Phoria UMC404HD](https://equipboard.com/items/behringer-u-phoria-umc404hd) | 4 in / 4 out | $139 (used ~$82) |
| Mid | [Behringer UMC1820](https://soundpro.com/products/behringer-000-b2j02-00010) | 8 in / 10 out | ~$229 |
| Reference | [MOTU UltraLite Mk5](https://equipboard.com/items/motu-ultralite-mk5) | 18 in / 22 out | ~$700 |

No-compromise alternative: [RME Fireface UCX II](https://markertek.com/product/fireface-ucx-ii/rme-fireface-ucx-ii-40-channel-192-khz-advanced-usb-2-0-audio-interface-with-midi-adat-aes-ebu-spdif-i-os),
~$1,699 — RME's drivers and long-term support are the industry benchmark.

## 3. Actuators: corner subwoofers (×2 budget, ×2–4 mid/reference)

Sealed alignments are preferred: smooth, minimum-phase low-frequency rolloff
(easier secondary paths, no port turbulence at the sustained drive levels ANC
demands). Output requirements are modest — the system only has to match the
drone's level, not fill a theater.

| Tier | Product | Type | Price (each) | Qty | Subtotal |
|------|---------|------|------:|:---:|------:|
| Budget | [Dayton Audio SUB-800](https://www.parts-express.com/Dayton-Audio-SUB-800-Powered-Subwoofer-300-627) 8″ | ported — accept the caveat at this price | ~$135 | 2 | ~$270 |
| Mid | [SVS SB-1000 Pro](https://hometechnologyreview.com/product/svs-sb-1000-pro-black-ash-sealed-box-subwoofer-12-325w/) 12″ | sealed, DSP + app control | ~$529 | 2 | ~$1,058 |
| Reference | [SVS SB-2000 Pro](https://www.soundandvision.com/content/svs-sb-2000-pro-subwoofer-review-specs) 12″ | sealed, 550 W | ~$800 | 4 | ~$3,200 |

Reference alternative: [Rythmik F12](https://hometheaterhifi.com/?p=74474)
(servo-controlled sealed 12″, ~$1,000–1,100 direct from rythmik.com) — the
servo feedback gives the most linear, lowest-distortion secondary path
available at consumer prices.

## 4. Error microphones (×4 budget, ×8 mid/reference)

Error mics do **not** need flat wideband response — only stable sensitivity
and adequate signal-to-noise ratio at the tone frequencies, since the loop
minimizes whatever they measure. This is why a $26 omni electret is genuinely
sufficient through the mid tier.

| Tier | Product | Price (each) | Qty | Subtotal |
|------|---------|------:|:---:|------:|
| Budget | [Behringer ECM8000](https://www.markertek.com/product/ecm8000/behringer-ecm8000-omnidirectional-measurement-condenser-microphone) omni electret | ~$26 | 4 | ~$104 |
| Mid | Behringer ECM8000, relative-calibrated against the UMIK-1 | ~$26 | 8 | ~$208 |
| Reference | [Beyerdynamic MM1](https://www.sweetwater.com/c105--Beyerdynamic_Omnidirectional_Condenser_Microphones) (±1.5 dB, 50 Hz–16 kHz) | ~$250 | 8 | ~$2,000 |

## 5. Calibrated measurement microphone (evidence track, R10)

One absolutely calibrated microphone for before/after spectra, acceptance
testing, and the landlord file. Separate from the error mics.

| Tier | Product | Price | Notes |
|------|---------|------:|-------|
| Budget | Smartphone + NIOSH SLM / Spectroid app | $0 | First-pass tone census only; not calibrated evidence. |
| Mid | [miniDSP UMIK-1](https://equipboard.com/items/minidsp-umik-1) (USB, individual cal file) | ~$108 | The REW-community standard; sufficient for R10. |
| Reference | [miniDSP UMIK-2](https://www.parts-express.com/MiniDSP-UMIK-2-Omni-directional-USB-Measurement-Calibrated-Microphone-230-3420) (32-bit, lower noise floor) | ~$230 | Alternative: [Earthworks M23R](https://equipboard.com/items/earthworks-m23r-omnidirectional-condenser-reference-measurement-microphone), ~$599. |

## 6. Reference sensor

The synthesized reference (tracked-tone oscillator, see
[spec](spec.qmd#tonal-structure-adaptive-notch-form)) is the preferred design —
perfect coherence, zero hardware. A physical sensor is only needed if the
tones turn out to wander too fast for the tracker.

| Tier | Product | Price | Notes |
|------|---------|------:|-------|
| Budget | None — synthesized reference | $0 | Preferred design. |
| Mid | Piezo contact pickup on window frame/wall, into a spare interface input | ~$20–40 | Uncalibrated is fine; only phase coherence matters. |
| Reference | [Digiducer 333D01](https://www.digikey.com/en/videos/a/amphenol-the-modal-shop/digiducer-usb-digital-accelerometer) USB IEPE accelerometer | ~$1,115 | Lab-grade; also quantifies structure-borne vibration for the landlord file. |

## 7. Cabling, stands, misc

XLR cables for every mic, mic clips/stands or camera-tripod mounts, line
cables to the subwoofers, a powered USB hub.

| Tier | Contents | Price |
|------|----------|------:|
| Budget | 4× 15 ft XLR, 2× RCA, zip ties, tape | ~$60 |
| Mid | 8× XLR, 4× line, 8 compact mic stands, USB hub | ~$150 |
| Reference | As mid, with quality cable and boom stands | ~$300 |

The **Mid tier is the recommended build**: it meets every requirement in the
[specification](spec.qmd) with margin, and the two SB-1000 Pros are
unembarrassing furniture if the landlord track succeeds and the ANC system
retires into a stereo.

## Selected build

The decided plan, fixed around a 4-in/4-out interface, four woofers at
≤ $250 each, and reuse of equipment on hand. Positions and mounting are on
the [Layout](layout.qmd) page.

| Component | Product | Qty | Unit | Ext. |
|---|---|:---:|---:|---:|
| Controller | Existing laptop/PC, Linux + PipeWire/JACK | 1 | $0 | $0 |
| Audio interface | [Behringer UMC404HD](https://equipboard.com/items/behringer-u-phoria-umc404hd) — 4 mic/line in (48 V), 4 balanced TRS out | 1 | $139 | $139 |
| Subwoofers | [PreSonus Eris Sub 8BT](https://www.sweetwater.com/store/detail/ErisStuSub8BT--presonus-eris-sub-8bt-8-inch-powered-bluetooth-studio-subwoofer) — 8″, 50 W RMS, 30–200 Hz | 4 | $200–250 | $800–1,000 |
| Error mics | [Samson C02](https://www.markertek.com/product/sam-co2/samson-c02-pencil-cardioid-condenser-microphones-pair) — 2 on hand + 1 new matched pair | 4 | — | ~$150 |
| Measurement mic | [miniDSP UMIK-1](https://equipboard.com/items/minidsp-umik-1) (calibration + evidence, R10) | 1 | ~$108 | ~$108 |
| Reference | Synthesized (tracked-tone oscillator) | — | $0 | $0 |
| **Total (key components)** | | | | **≈ $1,200–1,400** |

Why these choices fit:

- **Eris Sub 8BT.** Its 30–200 Hz band covers every measured line (59.0,
  105.8, 117.9, 120.0 Hz) with full headroom at the 59 Hz fundamental; the
  **balanced TRS input** takes the UMC404HD's TRS outputs directly with no
  adapters and best hum immunity; it has a polarity switch, and the
  variable low-pass reaches 130 Hz (set to maximum and never touched after
  secondary-path ID — note this soft-caps control authority between 130 and
  150 Hz, acceptable since no measured tone lives there). Street price
  [$249.95 at Sweetwater](https://www.sweetwater.com/store/detail/ErisStuSub8BT--presonus-eris-sub-8bt-8-inch-powered-bluetooth-studio-subwoofer),
  seen at [$199.99](https://electronicexpress.com/catalog/565780/presonus-2777500125-eris-sub-8bt-8-studio-monitor-subwoofer-bluetooth).
  Caveats: it is ported (port noise under sustained tonal drive — watch for
  broadband error-floor rise at high output); the **front cone is exposed
  (not cat-proof as shipped)** — mitigated by facing the driver into the
  corner, which is acoustically free at $\lambda \approx 5.8$ m (see
  [Layout](layout.qmd#subwoofers-four-corners-floor-level)); and the
  Power Saver auto-standby (engages after ~40 min of silence) must be
  verified to wake cleanly when the HVAC cycles back on — if it misbehaves,
  a −60 dBFS pilot dither on each output keeps the amps awake.
  Grille-protected alternatives at the price, if cat-proofing wins over the
  TRS convenience: [Dayton SUB-1200](https://www.parts-express.com/Dayton-Audio-SUB-1200-Powered-Subwoofer-300-629) (~$200, cloth grille) or
  [BIC America F12](https://www.ooberpad.com/blogs/audio-video-tips/ooberpad-india-reviews-the-bic-america-formula-f12-powered-subwoofer) (~$250 street when in stock, removable grille).
- **Samson C02 ×4.** Reusing the owned pair and adding one more
  [matched pair (~$140–180)](https://www.markertek.com/product/sam-co2/samson-c02-pencil-cardioid-condenser-microphones-pair)
  works: error mics need only stable sensitivity and SNR at the tones, the
  C02's 40 Hz–20 kHz band comfortably contains 59 Hz, and a ~56 dB tone
  dwarfs its 22 dB(A) self-noise. The cardioid pattern mixes in a
  pressure-gradient component, which is harmless so long as orientation is
  fixed — the mounting rules on the
  [Layout](layout.qmd#error-microphones-mounting) page handle this, plus
  the vibration isolation a pressure-gradient capsule particularly needs.
  The UMC404HD supplies the required +48 V phantom on all four inputs.
- **UMC404HD.** Exactly 4 phantom-powered mic inputs for the error array
  and 4 balanced line outputs for the subs, one clock domain for the whole
  loop, class-compliant under Linux. The UMIK-1 is USB and independent, so
  it costs no interface channels.

## Supporting items

Necessary for the build but not key components. Cable lengths assume the
corner runs of the [nominal layout](layout.qmd) (interface near the desk);
measure before ordering.

| Item | Qty | Est. | Notes |
|---|:---:|---:|---|
| XLR cables, 10–25 ft mix | 4 | $50 | error mics → interface; one per mic, routed along walls |
| Balanced ¼″ TRS–TRS cables, 10–25 ft mix | 4 | $60 | interface outs → sub TRS inputs |
| Weighted round-base mic stands | 2 | $60 | M4 free-standing; one spare/pillow-side |
| Clamp-on boom arms | 2 | $40 | M1/M2 on bed frame (through foam), M3 on desk |
| Pencil-mic shock mounts or foam clip pads | 4 | $30 | suspension $f_0 \lesssim 10$ Hz for ~−17 dB body vibration at 59 Hz |
| Subwoofer isolation pads | 4 | $50 | floor decoupling: rental, neighbors, structure-borne re-injection |
| Split-loom / floor cord covers | — | $25 | cat-proofing all floor runs |
| Power strips + extension cords | 2 | $25 | one per sub pair; interface + controller at desk |
| Gaffer tape, zip ties, marking tape | — | $15 | position/rotation marks at every mic and sub (re-ID discipline, R7) |
| **Subtotal** | | **≈ $355** | |

**Selected build grand total ≈ $1,550–1,750** including supporting items.

## Passive adjuncts (any tier)

Cheap, rental-compatible complements from the
[physics analysis](physics.qmd) — these attack leaks and modal $Q$, not the
tones themselves:

- Acoustic caulk (e.g., Green Glue sealant), ~$12/tube — window frame and
  penetration sealing
- Door weatherstripping / sweep kit, ~$15–25
- Mass-loaded vinyl, ~1 lb/ft², ~$2.50/ft² — removable window plug
  (~$80–150 for a typical window)
